learningObjective: Understand ONNX opset versioning as a semantic contract between producers and consumers.

canonicalClaims.claim: ONNX models declare specific opset versions via `opset_import`; consumers must implement the exact opset semantics to execute the model correctly. Op semantics can change across opset versions.
nonImplications: Does not imply every runtime must implement every version.
Does not imply each model has a single opset version; multiple domains each have their own.

misconceptions.claim: A runtime for opset 18 automatically implements semantics of opsets 1–17.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Runtimes must explicitly implement each version they claim to support.

misconceptions.claim: Opset only defines file format layout, not op semantics.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It defines op semantics; file format is separate.

misconceptions.claim: Every ONNX op has been stable since opset 1.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Attributes, new ops, and deprecations are documented across opsets.

implementationFacts: Version converters (onnx.version_converter) can move models between opsets when semantically compatible.
